name: Isometric Neck Lateral Flexion
summary: A self-resisted isometric exercise that strengthens the lateral cervical stabilizers without joint movement.

setup: Sit upright in a chair or stand tall with shoulders relaxed and spine neutral.
Place the palm of your hand against the side of your head, just above your ear.
steps: Gently push your head sideways into your hand while matching the pressure with your palm so no movement occurs.
Hold the isometric contraction steadily for the prescribed duration.
Gradually ease off the tension, rest briefly, and switch sides.
instructions.breathing: Breathe normally and continuously; do not hold your breath during the isometric hold.

common_faults.fault: Elevating or shrugging the working shoulder toward the ear.
common_faults.correction: Keep both shoulders pulled down and relaxed away from your ears.

common_faults.fault: Pushing too hard or forcefully jarring the neck.
common_faults.correction: Ramp tension up smoothly to a moderate, comfortable effort rather than maximum strain.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the neck to tilt or rotate during the press.
common_faults.correction: Keep the head aligned strictly centered with eyes looking straight ahead throughout the hold.

precautions: Stop immediately if you experience dizziness, sharp pain, or numbness radiating down the arm.
